T-001.Title: Interrupted-fold reconciliation, resume, and refusals with the final F313 behavior tests

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: `src/grace-cursor.ts` adds one pre-write reconciliation, `reconcileLooseWithLedger`, that compares the loose set against the durable ledger **before** any loose-only closure/hole check or `maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation` write, using independent payload comparison (`expectedLedgerEventAttributes` plus complete children), never the writer's own transform. For each of `injectFailureBeforeVerify` and `injectFailureAfterWrite`: after the throw the ledger holds exactly the one written epoch; a real `bun run ngrace cursor fold` retry exits 0, reuses that epoch, adds no new epoch and no synthesized `opened`, leaves each event exactly once, and empties `run/`. Repeated interruption is reachable on successive fresh epochs, driven independently for **each** hook: interrupt a logical epoch, recover it once, allocate a fresh epoch (ids above the recorded max), interrupt it at the same hook, recover it once; the ledger then holds exactly one copy of each logical epoch `[1,2]` and the first epoch's bytes are unchanged. A third, empty fold returns the same last epoch with `eventCount 0`. Partial verified deletion is resumed, not treated as conflict: inject the post-write failure (`injectFailureAfterWrite`); capture the complete `run-ledger.xml` bytes; then delete the first event of the verified set in the shipped sequential delete-loop order (`src/grace-cursor.ts:1522-1530`, the `unlinkSync` at `:1529`); then run the real CLI retry; it exits 0, reuses the interrupted epoch, leaves no loose files, one recorded `opened` only, and the captured `run-ledger.xml` bytes exactly unchanged, with the recorded payload independently equal under `expectedLedgerEventAttributes` plus children. Byte identity and semantic payload equivalence are distinct claims and both are asserted. Initial-state controls: a prior completed epoch stays byte-identical across a later recovery; a fresh-only allocated set (ids matching no recorded event) folds normally into the next epoch. The final repository tests are added first and re-driven red on the committed base for behavioral reasons, not import/type/load failure: `bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-cursor.test.ts` is 218 pass / 10 fail (the nine F313 behavioral guards plus the write-surface inventory pin) on base `0ad7cb4e49b1bb5d930b27732f2978fa66221371`, and 228 pass / 0 fail after this task. The production change adds exactly one `unlinkSync(contained.absolutePath)` contained-path delete site, so the write-surface inventory pin moves `cursorContained` 2→3 and `callSites` 9→10.

A genuine payload conflict — a loose event whose id matches a recorded event but whose canonical payload differs under `expectedLedgerEventAttributes` plus children — makes the fold exit non-zero with a message naming the id and the mismatch, writes no new epoch, and leaves the recorded bytes byte-identical. A loose event whose id matches an event in an **older** recorded epoch is refused, naming the id and the older epoch; untouched older epochs are never rewritten and no synthesized `opened` is fabricated for an already-recorded epoch. A payload-matching subset of the **last** recorded epoch (the partial-deletion state) is not a conflict and resumes per the first criterion. Both refusals are backed by a byte-complete recursive project-tree snapshot (directory entries, symlinks, relative paths, types, per-file sha256) unchanged (`treeDiff` `[]`), and the base directions are discriminating: the base does not name the id on a conflicting loose `opened` (it refuses with `unterminated range for w0`) and folds an older-epoch id reuse at exit 0 into `Epoch-3` with a non-empty `treeDiff`.

The post-ledger write-verify-delete boundary (`C-RUN-LEDGER` `AC-FOLD-ORDERING`, **never** labelled F158) is preserved: a fold interrupted after its ledger write may leave the written ledger and engine-authored loose events, but the refuse path removes, renumbers, and rewrites no `run/` event and no recorded epoch it did not itself write, and a subsequent successful fold recovers that evidence idempotently. After `injectFailureAfterWrite`, the written ledger holds `Epoch-1`; the real-CLI retry and a second retry each exit 0 and leave the written `run-ledger.xml` byte-identical with no accumulated evidence, whereas the base rewrites the ledger by appending `Epoch-2`.
